nodes.label: PyChrono Conda Package Installation
nodes.rationale: Recommended path because prebuilt conda packages install in a single step across Linux/Windows/MacOS and multiple Python 3 versions; a dedicated conda environment is advised so dependency resolution stays isolated. Trade-off: cascade, vsg3d and ROS modules are absent from the conda build.

nodes.label: Building PyChrono from the C++ API
nodes.rationale: Preferred way to get the most up-to-date PyChrono and the only way to obtain cascade, vsg3d and ROS modules, at the cost of a more complicated build requiring the full Chrono C++ source.

nodes.label: PYTHONPATH Requirement for Source Builds
nodes.rationale: A source-built PyChrono lands in the build tree's bin/ directory rather than site-packages, so PYTHONPATH must be extended to include it or imports fail.

nodes.label: AMD ROCm CPU PyChrono Build
nodes.rationale: CPU PyChrono can be built without the NVIDIA CUDA toolkit so machines running PyTorch ROCm on AMD Instinct/Radeon GPUs are not forced into a CUDA install; Eigen3 and SWIG remain prerequisites and ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES matters on multi-GPU hosts.
